transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07 09:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Gomez (Redwood AE), Devon Li (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Novapay Platform), Maya Chen (Novapay ML Infra), Tom Erickson (Novapay SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick sync on latency tweaks and kernel tests; some audio dropouts; see action items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check  can you hear me okay?
[00:04] Raj: Yeah, loud and clear.
[00:06] Maya: Yep, good here.
[00:12] Alicia: Great. Today's pulse is latency tuning  specifically TTFT, how streaming's behaving in your POC, sequence length impacts, and kernel choices. Devon's going to walk through the recent runs.
[00:25] Devon: Cool, I'll share my screen  um  just a heads up the chart labels got munged in the export so model names maybe truncated.
[00:34] Tom: That's fine, we mainly care about patterns.
[00:40] Devon: Alright first slide, TTFT baseline with hosted config: p50 TTFT was around 120ms, p95 ~320ms, p99 ~480ms. These are without streaming enabled and with batch size small.
[00:54] Raj: Is that across our 2k sample or the 10k run?
[00:58] Devon: That was the 2k quick pass. The 10k mixed workload shows similar p50 but p95 moved a little due to longer sequences.
[01:08] Maya: When you say streaming disabled, do you mean we waited for full generation before sending any tokens back?
[01:13] Devon: Correct  non-streamed. We then tested streaming (chunked at token flush) and saw TTFT drop to ~70ms p50 but p95 improved only a bit because our model spends time on first attention block for long sequences.
[01:26] Raj: Interesting  so streaming improves perceived latency but heavy seq lengths still hit p95.
[01:31] Alicia: Right, perceived latency vs true end-to-end matters for UX. We should map to your SLOs. What are you targeting again?
[01:38] Tom: We want interactive responses  TTFT under 100ms p50 and p95 under 400ms. p99 ideally under 700 if possible.
[01:46] Alicia: Okay that gives us a clear target.
[01:50] Devon: On kernel choices  we ran two profiles: default cuBLAS-ish kernels and an optimized Triton-like path with custom fused kernels. The optimized kernels reduced token-step time by ~15% for medium sequences (<=256), but for long sequences (>512) the scheduler overhead pushed gains down to ~5%.
[02:10] Maya: Hmm, that aligns with our seq distribution where a lot of user requests are in the 200-400 range, but we have a tail to 1200 tokens for long sessions.
[02:19] Raj: Can we apply mixed kernels depending on sequence length?
[02:22] Devon: Yes, the runtime can route by sequence-length thresholds; we can set a policy to use optimized kernels up to 512 and fall back beyond that. There's some cost in switching though.
[02:31] Tom: Any memory impact? The optimized kernels increased peak VRAM by a bit right?
[02:36] Devon: Slightly higher recall buffers  ~4% memory overhead in our tests. Not huge but worth noting for Dedicated.
[02:43] Alicia: Let's capture that as a tradeoff: latency vs memory and cost.
[02:47] Devon: Next, KV cache and prefix caching: enabling KV cache for repeated prefixes dropped per-token compute by about 12% on average for our chat traces. For conversations with repeated system prompts it's bigger.
[02:58] Maya: That sounds promising; our flows have a shared system prompt for auth checks so could be big win.
[03:04] Raj: How does that interact with streaming? Any double-counting of savings?
[03:07] Devon: They stack. Streaming reduces time-to-first-token while KV cache reduces per-token compute once the KV pairs are hit. But note, first token still needs full initial pass.
[03:17] Maya: Any errors with KV invalidation when users switch contexts? We have multi-tenant sessions.
[03:21] Devon: There's a TTL and explicit invalidation API. Need to ensure your session manager calls invalidate when context changes. We can help add wrappers.
[03:29] Raj: Ok we'll coordinate on that.
[03:33] [00:03:34 audio glitch]
[03:37] Devon: Sorry, dropped a bit  continuing. The benchmark plan: we'll run two 10k mixes  one streaming enabled with KV cache, one streaming disabled but with optimized kernel to compare TTFT and p95/p99.
[03:51] Tom: What's the target distribution? Our prod-ish mix is 70% short chats (<128), 20% mid (128-512), 10% long (>512).
[03:59] Devon: Good to know  we'll mirror that. Also we'll capture client-side perceived TTFT by measuring first byte at edge vs server-side compute times.
[04:09] Maya: Can we get the raw logs to run our SLO calc?
[04:12] Devon: Yes we'll share raw logs. We'll scrub any PII; it's perf metrics only.
[04:17] Raj: On error modes  what's fallback if optimized kernel fails?
[04:20] Devon: Runtime can fallback to safe kernel path. We saw rare hangs when we pushed kernel-level quantization combos; fallback was auto and requests completed with slight latency bump. Logs mark the fallback event.
[04:33] Alicia: Good to know. Any concern re: model variants? If we do quantized model vs full-precision, does that change kernel behavior?
[04:41] Devon: Yeah quantization interacts  some fused kernels are tuned for int8 paths; float16 may be different. We'll include both quantization settings in the bench.
[04:50] Raj: Cost question  will optimized kernels be more expensive on Dedicated?
[04:55] Devon: Not inherently; they trade compute time for higher utilization. If peak memory grows we may need larger instances which can shift cost. We'll quantify per-token cost in the bench.
[05:05] Tom: For our procurement justification we need per-10k-run cost delta and expected monthly cost at 1M requests.
[05:12] Alicia: We'll provide a cost spreadsheet after the bench runs.
[05:17] Devon: One other nuance  streaming has different network patterns; more small packets. In some of your regions we saw slightly higher egress jitter which can inflate TTFT at the edge.
[05:29] Maya: That's concerning  our EU edge is bandwidth constrained sometimes.
[05:33] Devon: We can simulate regional variance in the bench or apply packet coalescing at the edge to mitigate.
[05:39] Raj: Can Redwood support SSO/SAML for access to the console where we'll see traces?
[05:44] Alicia: Yes, SSO and RBAC are supported; for Private deployments we can integrate with your IdP. We'll send the docs.
[05:50] Tom: Security docs please  SOC 2 and audit logs, and KMS integration for keys.
[05:54] Alicia: We'll attach our security pack and a short one-pager on KMS options.
[05:59] [00:06:00 background typing noise]
[06:03] Devon: Back to kernel routing  we can do canary rollouts so half of traffic goes to optimized kernel to measure real-world impact before full switch. That might be safer given tail behavior.
[06:15] Maya: That would be ideal. Can we route by path too? Some endpoints are latency-sensitive, others are batch.
[06:21] Devon: Yes route by route or by model route. The console supports per-route rollout configs.
[06:27] Raj: Great. Regarding metrics, can Redwood export per-token compute time, queue wait, and network send time separately?
[06:34] Devon: Yes  per-token compute and queue wait times, plus client-side first-byte timestamps if you instrument the SDK.
[06:42] Tom: We'll schedule an infra-level access for traces.
[06:45] Alicia: Quick recap  action items: Redwood runs two 10k benches (streaming+KV and non-stream+optimized kernel) and shares logs; Novapay exports prompt distribution and enables tracing. Follow-up the week of 7/20.
[06:58] Raj: Sounds good.
[07:00] Maya: Quick question  do you have guidance on sequence-length bucketing for routing thresholds?
[07:05] Devon: Empirically we recommend thresholds at 128, 256, 512. Above that treat as long-tail and route to capacity that tolerates higher token cost. But it's tunable.
[07:16] Raj: I'll take that to product.
[07:19] Tom: Also please include the p99 breakdown by seq-bucket in the bench output.
[07:23] Devon: Will do.
[07:25] [00:07:26 brief crosstalk]
[07:30] Alicia: Any blockers on next steps?
[07:32] Maya: None from our side; will push sample export by Friday.
[07:36] Raj: We'll circle up on TTL/invalidation for KV.
[07:40] Devon: I'll start the bench run tomorrow and aim to have preliminary graphs by next Wednesday.
[07:46] Alicia: Great. Thanks everyone  we'll email the security docs and the cost spreadsheet after the runs.
[07:52] Raj: Thanks.
[07:54] Maya: Bye.
[07:56] Tom: Bye all.

End of transcript.
